figures.caption: Figure 6: (a) τ across four A40 models and five datasets grouped by GOOSE’s affinity. CV below each column shows cross-model coefficient of variation. (b) Per-model mean τeq5/τiso across 25 settings; all bars exceed 1.0, confirming spine dominance (Pearson r=0.91).

Figure 3: Wall-clock speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding across five models and five benchmarks. All methods are lossless (greedy decoding, identical output). Speedup values for GOOSE are annotated above each bar. Full per-benchmark results including compression ratio (τ ) are reported in Table 3. †Vicuna-33B runs on 2×A100-40GB; all others on a single A40.

Figure 5: Acceptance heterogeneity across five benchmarks. (a) Mean p̂s and p̂t per benchmark (averaged over 5 models); the ratio N× above each bar pair quantifies the gap. (b) Heterogeneity ratio p̂s/p̂t per model×benchmark (25 settings).

Figure 4: (a) GOOSE’s mean τ decomposed into the best standalone baseline max(τPLD, τTR) (gray) and the synergy gain from the spine-tree topology (green); the gain ranges from +16% (Vicuna-13B) to +45% (Llama-3-8B). (b) Hyperparameter sensitivity (Qwen3-8B): each panel sweeps one parameter; τ plateaus at B≥60 and D≥6, and varies by fewer than 0.6 τ units across r and ρ.

Figure 2: GOOSE pipeline overview. From anchor ., Stage 1 draws from a unified candidate pool: context matching produces the spine (blue), the adjacency table supplies branches (orange). Stage 2 verifies all candidates via one LLM forward pass. Stage 3 selects the longest accepted path via a greedy walk, discovering spine continuation: “2”→ “)” extends beyond the spine mismatch, yielding 8 tokens per call.
